tips.title: Bitcoin tips
tips.subtitle: Give bitcoin as a link or on paper. Whoever holds the note owns what is on it — nobody custodies it in between, not even us.

empty.title: No batches yet
empty.text: A batch mints notes from your wallet. Each one is funded straight away, and you can send it as a link or print a sheet to hand out.

batch.missingHint: Batches live in this browser only, because they hold the secrets that unlock the money. Open the link on the device you created it on.
batch.reprintTitle: Keep this browser until you have printed
batch.reprintText: The note secrets are stored here and nowhere else. Losing them does not lose the money — unclaimed notes return to your wallet when they expire — but you will not be able to reprint the sheet.
batch.linkText: A note can be handed over as a link instead of printed — the person opening it needs no wallet and no account. Send each link to one person only: whoever opens it first takes the money. The link is the money, so send it the way you would send cash.

new.title: New batch of tips
new.amountHint: About {fiat} per note at today's rate.
new.countHint: Nine notes fit on one A4 sheet.
new.expiryHint: A note nobody claims returns to your wallet by itself when this runs out. You cannot take it back earlier — that is what makes the paper trustworthy.
new.totalHint: Leaves your wallet now, note by note. Anything nobody claims comes back at the end.
new.fundingHint: Do not close this tab — each note is funded separately.
new.walletNeeded: Open your wallet first: this batch is funded from it.
new.insufficient: Not enough in your wallet for {sats} sats.

print.title: Print tips
print.hint: A4, margins none, background graphics on.
print.about: Bitcoin is open-source digital money. It moves worldwide, in seconds, with no bank in the middle. This paper is a real wallet — whoever holds it owns what is on it.
print.returns: Unclaimed, it returns to the sender by itself. Nobody holds it in the meantime.

claim.title: Your bitcoin tip
claim.invalid: This link has no tip on it
claim.invalidHint: Open the full link you were sent, or scan the QR code on the paper note.
claim.emptyHint: It was already claimed, or it expired and went back to whoever gave it to you.
claim.claimHint: This unlocks the money into the wallet that this note is a key to.
claim.keepIt: You can leave it here — this note is the wallet, and it keeps working. Move it to your own wallet whenever you like.
claim.destinationHint: A Lightning invoice or address is cheapest. An on-chain address works too, but the network fee can be more than a small tip is worth.
claim.sentHint: It is on its way to the wallet you gave. This note is spent — the link and the paper no longer hold anything.
claim.aboutText: Bitcoin is digital money that moves directly between people, anywhere in the world, with no bank in the middle. This note is already yours: leave it where it is and come back later, or move it to any wallet you like. Neither needs an account with us.
claim.remembered: Filled in from your last cash-out.
claim.tooSmall: This note is too small to send over Lightning — the fee costs more than it holds. Try a Spark address instead.

sync.offHint: Minted a batch on another device? Batches stay where they were created unless wallet sync is on.
sync.keyMismatch: Wallet sync is on, but the wallet on this device differs from the one that synced. Restore the same 12-word seed to see batches from your other devices.
